#Part A

#Question A1A
scores <- c(88, 72, 95, 60, 83, 91)
names(scores) <- c("Ana", "Ben", "Carl", "Dina", "Eve", "Felix")
scores

#Question A1B
sort(scores)                        
sort(scores, decreasing = TRUE)

#Question A1C
sorted_asc <- sort(scores)
print(sorted_asc)

#Question A1D
subjects   <- c("Science", "Math", "English", "Filipino", "PE")
incomplete <- c(85, NA, 90, 70, NA, 95)

#Question A1E
sort(subjects)

#Question A1F
sort(incomplete)

#Question A2
#Yes. As shown in Part A3, the names (Ana, Ben, Carl, etc.) moved along with their corresponding scores after sorting.

#Question A3
#If your data has NA entries and you run sort(incomplete)[1] to get the lowest score, R quietly drops the NAs first and returns 70. You get a result with no warning

#Question A4
order(scores)
sort(scores)

#Question A5
name    <- c("Ana", "Ben", "Cid", "Dex", "Eli", "Fay", "Gio")
score   <- c(78, 92, 85, 92, 67, 88, 74)
section <- c("A", "B", "A", "B", "A", "B", "A")

students <- data.frame(name, score, section)
students

#Question A5A
students[order(students$score), ]

#Question A5B
students[order(students$score, decreasing = TRUE), ]

#Question A6
#order() returns the index positions of elements arranged from smallest to largest — not the values themselves. So 4 means “the smallest value is at position 4 (Dina = 60)”, 2 means “the next smallest is at position 2 (Ben = 72).

#Question A7
#sort() only works on a single vector. If you ran sort(students), R would throw an error or behave unexpectedly because a data frame has multiple columns. order() is the correct tool because it returns index positions, and those positions can be used to reorder all columns simultaneously via students[order(...), ].

#Question A8 (Coding)
scores <- c(78, 92, 85, 92, 67, 88, 74)
names(scores) <- c("Ana", "Ben", "Cid", "Dex", "Eli", "Fay", "Gio")

cbind(scores, rank(scores))

#Question A8A
#Both Ben and Dex received rank 6.5.

#Question A8B
#Ben and Dex both scored 92, which are the 6th and 7th highest values when sorted ascending. By default, R’s rank() uses average ranking for ties.

#Question A8A Dataframe
sales <- data.frame(
  employee   = c("Rey", "Sam", "Tin", "Uma", "Val"),
  units_sold = c(120, 145, 145, 98, 130)
)

sales$rank <- rank(-sales$units_sold)

sales

#Question A8B Dataframe
sales[order(sales$units_sold, decreasing = TRUE), ]
